facts.statement: The known fossil material of Sphenosuchus consists mainly of a well-preserved skull, with only some forelimb elements and isolated hind limb parts found.
facts.quote: The skull is preserved very well but other than elements of the forelimb and isolated parts of the hind limb, the Sphenosuchus material is incomplete.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus was one of the largest early crocodylomorphs, with a skull length of 192 mm and a total body length estimated at 1.4 meters.
facts.quote: Out of the early crocodylomorphs, Sphenosuchus was one of the largest. The skull was 192 mm in the length and the body an estimated total length of 1.4 m.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus is considered to have been a carnivorous and cursorial animal.
facts.quote: This genus is considered to have been carnivorous and cursorial.

facts.statement: The dentary of Sphenosuchus held roughly fourteen teeth, with about one-third of them being larger than the rest.
facts.quote: The dentary is slender and moderate in length, it appears to have roughly fourteen teeth with a third of them being larger than the others.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus was first thoroughly described in 1972 by the British paleontologist Alick Walker in a paper published in the journal Nature.
facts.quote: Sphenosuchus was first thoroughly described in 1972 by the British palaeontologist Alick Walker, in a paper in the journal Nature.

facts.statement: In 1927, Broom believed that Sphenosuchus was a pseudosuchian closely related to the lineage leading to true crocodiles.
facts.quote: Broom believed, in 1927, with the evidence present in the specimens, that Sphenosuchus is a pseudosuchian which is well along the line that leads to the true crocodiles.

facts.statement: Broom suggested in 1927 that Sphenosuchus represents a pseudosuchian well along the evolutionary line leading to modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Broom believed, in 1927, with the evidence present in the specimens, that Sphenosuchus is a pseudosuchian which is well along the line that leads to the true crocodiles.

facts.statement: In 1995, Johann Welman argued that Sphenosuchus brain case structures were too specialized to make it the sister group of birds, despite earlier hypotheses linking the two.
facts.quote: In 1995 Johann Welman published a paper "Euparkeria and the origin of birds". where he argues that while Sphenosuchus had been thought to potentially be related to birds he finds the brain case structures of Sphenosuchus to be too specialized to be the sister group of birds.

facts.statement: Johann Welman noted a difference in the eustachian system, observing that crocodiles and Sphenosuchus have a median system while birds do not.
facts.quote: Another feature he found to be different was the eustachian system. Crocodiles and Sphenosuchus have a median eustachian system while birds do not.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus lived during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages, approximately 201.4 to 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus was probably quadrupedal but may have been capable of facultative bipedalism.
facts.quote: It was probably quadrupedal, but may have been a facultative biped.

facts.statement: In Sphenosuchus, the primary head of the quadrate bone meets the prootic and squamosal bones.
facts.quote: The primary head of the quadrate meets the prootic and squamosal.

facts.statement: The jugal bone in Sphenosuchus is large, forming the entire lower orbital margin and almost the whole of the lower temporal bar.
facts.quote: The jugal is a large bone forming the whole of the lower orbital and almost all of the lower temporal bar.

facts.statement: The parietal bone in Sphenosuchus forms nearly the entire intertemporal region and the majority of the occiput.
facts.quote: The parietal is a good sized element forming nearly the entire intertemporal region along with the majority of the occiput.

facts.statement: There is no parietal foramen present in the skull of Sphenosuchus.
facts.quote: There is no parietal foramen present.

facts.statement: Evidence from a forelimb suggests Sphenosuchus had a carpus with elongated radius and ulna bones that were metacarpal-like in structure.
facts.quote: From one of the forelimbs it appears that Sphenosuchus has a carpus with the radius and ulna elongated and metacarpal like in structure.

facts.statement: In Sphenosuchus, metatarsal I is reduced, metatarsals II and IV are symmetrical, and metatarsal III is the longest.
facts.quote: Metatarsal I is reduced, II and IV are symmetrical and III is the longest.

facts.statement: The posttemporal fenestrae in Sphenosuchus are relatively small compared to other early archosaurs, despite size variation among the group.
facts.quote: The post temporal fenestrae are known for the Sphenosuchus with the sizes being very variable among early archosaurs but rather small in size for Sphenosuchus

facts.statement: The skull of Sphenosuchus is similar to that of crocodiles but is slightly deeper.
facts.quote: The skull is similar to those of crocodiles however it is slightly deeper.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus acutus is the type species and the only described species within the genus Sphenosuchus.
facts.quote: The type species, Sphenosuchus acutus is the only described species in this genus.

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: Parent group: Crocodylomorpha

facts.statement: Sphenosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
